checks.reference_relief_evidence: DW-P0-A5 (#32, 2026-09-11 Phase-2 activation): reference-point elevation relief (max-min of the supplied --reference elevations), a geometric signal independent of model output. PRIMARY threshold source - the SAME statistic used at runtime: PHASE2_RED_FLAGS/outputs/metrics/E_hilly_risk_signal_experiment.json's sampled_reference_range_m, per RANSAC seed, over the same 10 sampled reference points used in that seed's fit (5 seeds x 5 scenes, all included regardless of downstream fit validity - pre-fit threshold, no post-fit conditioning). Known-good (4 Vaihingen areas, 20 samples): 7.774-44.355 m. Known-failure (Mount Adams, 5 samples): 130.650-266.360 m. No overlap (good_max=44.355 m < failure_min=130.650 m). Frozen midpoint rule: threshold = (good_max + failure_min) / 2 = 87.50 m (exact 87.50271606445312). In-sample: 0 known-good samples above threshold, 0 known-failure samples at/below it - screening evidence on n=1 known-failure scene, not a validated error rate. Full derivation: 10_DOCUMENTATION/evidence/DW_P0_A5_hilly_relief_gate/reference_relief_threshold_analysis.json. CORROBORATING CONTEXT ONLY (does not derive this threshold, both are DENSE whole-patch/full-AOI statistics, not the sparse statistic above): PHASE2_RED_FLAGS/outputs/metrics/E_hilly_terrain_eval.json's per-patch oracle results (observed lower-relief patches relief_m <= 118.54 m -> RMSE 3.03-23.89 m; observed high-relief/high-error patches relief_m >= 222.80 m -> RMSE 41.66-62.33 m), and (internal note, not included) SS3/SS8's full-AOI comparison (Vaihingen area6 67.16 m vs Mount Adams 370.4 m) - related evidence from the same preserved data, not independent confirmations of each other. Provisional floor, not a validated cutoff - see HILLY_RELIEF_THRESHOLD_M. A LOW sparse reading is NOT proof of safety outside this preserved dataset - a hilly scene sampled in a narrow elevation band could understate its own relief and pass undetected. Disclosed, open limitation.
